Most teams still don't automate agent evaluation. 62% don't in the AIQ Report survey of teams of all sizes, and 48% don't in the TechWire survey of companies with more than 200 employees. - **Adoption is low and depends on who you ask.**

- **LLM-as-judge is mostly uncalibrated.** Only 11% of teams using a judge have calibrated it against human labels. The rest treat judge scores as ground truth. [aiqreport.com](https://aiqreport.com/2026/state-of-agent-evals) This is a single-source claim.
- **Golden sets are too small.** The median is 22 tasks. AIQ says that is too small to separate a good agent from a mediocre one with useful confidence. [aiqreport.com](https://aiqreport.com/2026/state-of-agent-evals) This is also single-source, and the "too small" judgment is AIQ's opinion, not a measured result.

[northgate-analytics](https://northgate-analytics.example/notes/agent-eval-market-sizing) Treat it as `[UNVERIFIED]`.

| | AIQ Report | TechWire |
|---|---|---|
| Published | 2026-03-12 | 2026-06-02 |
| Sample | 1,204 teams, all sizes, recruited via practitioner newsletters | 890 orgs, over 200 employees |

3. **Measurement-validity gap:** uncalibrated judges (only 11% calibrate) and small golden sets (median 22) mean many reported scores carry little signal.

It says the 2030 market size ($2.4–4.1bn) depends almost entirely on whether evaluation consolidates into observability suites or stays standalone. That means even the analysts treat it as an open question. My searches turned up no vendor announcements, acquisitions or analyst forecasts on consolidation.

## Key Findings
- **The market is an open bet.** Northgate estimates the combined "agent evaluation and observability tooling" market at about $310M in 2025 and models $2.4–4.1bn for 2030. It says the spread is driven "almost entirely" by the consolidation question. The segment breakdown and vendor shares are paywalled, so I couldn't read the reasoning. [Northgate](https://northgate-analytics.example/notes/agent-eval-market-sizing) `[single source, abstract only]`
- **Most teams don't do automated evaluation yet.**
  - **AIQ Report (March 2026):** 62% of 1,204 teams run no automated evaluation. [AIQ](https://aiqreport.com/2026/state-of-agent-evals)
  - **TechWire (June 2026):** 48% of 890 organisations, all with more than 200 employees. [TechWire](https://techwire.example/research/agent-eval-adoption-2026)
  - The two figures aren't in conflict. They sampled different populations, and TechWire attributes the gap partly to that.
  - Both say adoption is rising.
- **Evaluation practice is immature.** Only 9% (AIQ) to 13% (TechWire) of teams score trajectories rather than just outcomes. Only 11% of LLM-as-judge users calibrate against human labels, and the median golden set is 22 tasks. [AIQ](https://aiqreport.com/2026/state-of-agent-evals), [TechWire](https://techwire.example/research/agent-eval-adoption-2026) Buyers are still working out what good evaluation looks like. So the category's boundaries aren't settled, and I'd expect them to move.
- **At least one standalone vendor is positioning around the OpenTelemetry boundary.** EvalTools (Berlin, 31 employees) describes itself as "not an observability vendor" and says it integrates with OpenTelemetry rather than replacing it. Its pitch centres on golden datasets, CI merge gates and calibrated judges. [EvalTools](https://evaltools.io/about) `[vendor self-description, not independent evidence]`

## Detailed Analysis
**What the evidence supports**

| Question | Evidence | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| Is the outcome genuinely undetermined as of Oct 2026? | Northgate's framing only | Low (one source, paywalled) |
| Is demand growing? | Two surveys agree on direction | Medium |
| Are buyers mature enough to know what they need? | No, per both surveys | Medium |
| Have observability incumbents shipped or bought evaluation? | Not found | None |

**Plausible arguments (my reasoning, not sourced findings)**
- *For consolidation:* tracing data already sits in observability tools, and evaluation could become a feature on top of it. EvalTools' OpenTelemetry integration suggests the data layer is shared.
- *For staying standalone:* evaluation work happens before release (golden datasets, CI gates, judge calibration). That is a different workflow and buyer from production monitoring. This is a hypothesis. I found nothing that tests it.
- *Likeliest mixed outcome:* trace collection commoditises into observability, while dataset and judge tooling stays specialised or gets acquired. I couldn't verify this either.

**Sources I excluded**
- "The 17 Best Agent Evaluation Platforms in 2026" (top-ai-tools-daily.example) is a promotional listicle. Its "91% of AI agents fail" claim has no cited source. I did not use it.

**Gaps**
- I found no data on whether Datadog, New Relic, Grafana, Dynatrace or similar vendors have shipped agent evaluation. I also found no acquisitions of evaluation startups and no funding data for Braintrust, LangSmith or Arize. The search index returned the same handful of pages for every query. These gaps reflect my search tool's coverage, not proof that nothing has happened.

1. **Treat "consolidate vs. standalone" as unresolved.** Don't present either outcome as the expected one in anything the owner publishes or teaches.
2. **Verify the vendor facts directly before relying on any conclusion.** Check the product and changelog pages of the major observability vendors for evaluation features, and look for acquisition announcements. If you want, I can run a deeper pass on those pages.
3. **Get the Northgate full note if the answer matters commercially.** It's the only source that models both scenarios. The paywall is the main obstacle.
4. **For the owner's Acme Training AI/QA teaching, this is a useful angle.** The surveys show evaluation practice is weak: untested judges, tiny golden sets, and little trajectory scoring. That holds whichever way the category goes, so teaching evaluation methodology doesn't depend on the answer. This is my inference from the survey data.
